title: Unintended canary promotion from health-signal noise; pinlock mitigation & capacity follow-up
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a routine model rollout, a canary unexpectedly auto-promoted after noisy health signals caused the promotion policy evaluator to exceed the promotion threshold. The promotion resulted in a partial capacity surge on Dedicated pools and left several customer routes pinned to a newer model version due to a pinlock race in the rollback controller. This ticket tracks the post-incident follow-ups: immediate mitigations applied, investigation notes, and long-term actions to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-18T02:12:00Z - Canary rollout started for model-v2026-02-18-A with weight=5%
2026-02-18T02:23:30Z - Automated health evaluator reported transient OK spikes from a noisy latency metric (p50 smoothing window misconfigured)
2026-02-18T02:25:10Z - Promotion decision executed by evaluator (threshold crossed) -> promoter set route weight to 40%
2026-02-18T02:27:00Z - Autoscaler reacted to increased QPS on Dedicated pools, attempted scale-up but hit pre-provision limits; tail latency increased for some tenants

2026-02-18T02:35:45Z - Rollback controller attempted to revert to pinned version but encountered a pinlock: simultaneous promotion and rollback requests caused a version-pin state where routes remained partially promoted
2026-02-18T02:50:00Z - Incident declared; mitigation actions applied (manually forced rollout to previous stable, temporary capacity increase, and turned off auto-promote)
2026-02-18T03:40:00Z - Customer-facing impact contained; follow-up investigation started
root_cause: Two converging failures: (1) the health evaluator used a smoothing window and metric selection that made p50 latency spikes look like a steady improvement, causing false positives for the automated promotion policy; (2) the rollback controller's optimistic concurrency logic did not handle concurrent promotion events, resulting in a pinlock where route state could not fully revert without manual intervention.
immediate_mitigation: Disabled auto-promotion flag for all model rollouts (feature flag: rollout.auto_promote=false)
Manually forced affected routes back to stable model version and cleared pin state via force-unpin endpoint
Provisioned burst capacity on Dedicated pools for 90 minutes to relieve tail latency while rollbacks completed
Created ad-hoc alert for evaluator anomaly rates and pinned-state increases
long_term_actions: ENG - Update promotion evaluator to use multi-metric consensus (latency p50+p95, error rate) and add hysteresis; owner: Jonah Rivera; due: 2026-03-15
ENG - Harden rollback controller to use compare-and-swap with backoff and a dead-letter queue for conflicting operations; owner: Priya Nambiar; due: 2026-03-22
ENG/OPS - Add a soft-stop feature in Console to block auto-promote during capacity-constrained windows and show upcoming promotions; owner: Ops Team Lead (Marcus Lee); due: 2026-03-08
ENG - Add canary promotion dry-run mode that runs evaluator without committing route changes; owner: Lina Chen; due: 2026-03-10
SRE - Increase burst scaling headroom thresholds for Dedicated by 15% and document failure modes; owner: SRE Team; due: 2026-03-05
DX - Update rollout runbook with new checklist items (verify metrics, capacity headroom, manual override steps) and attach screenshots; owner: Maya Ortiz; due: 2026-03-12
PM - Postmortem review with customers impacted and SLA review; owner: Evan Brooks; due: 2026-03-18
notes: Investigation found evaluator config drift: canary-evaluator.smoothing_window was set to 3 samples instead of the standard 12
Promoter logs show rapid consecutive promotion attempts; promoter did not checkpoint an in-flight operation before applying next weight update
Rollback controller tracks 'pinned_by' metadata which was set by both automated and manual actions; necessary to separate automated_owner vs human_owner fields
Capacity surge was bounded to 7 Dedicated clusters; no host-level OOMs detected
